subject: Implementation orchestration: enterprise access checklist & staging plan
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Implementation orchestration: enterprise access checklist & staging plan

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. As discussed, I'm attaching a concise implementation checklist so we can align responsibilities and cutover windows.

Quick asks to unblock the first week of work:
- SAML metadata (IdP entity + certificate) or IdP metadata URL
- SCIM admin account with service principal (email + least-privilege role)
- IP allowlist ranges for both staging and prod (we'll put staging behind a temporary VPN/IP tunnel)
- Desired service account naming convention and token rotation cadence

I've attached: implementation-checklist.xlsx (worksheet: responsibilities, sequencing, preflight).
Proposed next steps:
1) You share SAML metadata + SCIM admin by Tue 9/16
2) We validate against our staging instance and confirm attribute mappings
3) Schedule a dry-run cutover in staging the week of 9/20, production cutover the following week (subject to approvals)

If that works, can you confirm resource owners for SSO and for SCIM provisioning? Also, please confirm any procurement/compliance approvals that might delay access to network ranges.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a meeting invite once I have the two owners.

Best,

Mateo Alvarez
Customer Implementation Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: implementation-checklist.xlsx]

From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@acmecorp.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation orchestration: enterprise access checklist & staging plan

Hi Mateo,

Thanks — appreciate the checklist. Attaching our IdP metadata and a partial IP list for staging (we're still confirming prod ranges with networking). A few notes:
- SAML metadata attached: acme-saml-metadata.xml
- SCIM admin: scim-admin@acmecorp.com (we will create a dedicated service principal; please provide exact scope you need)
- IP allowlist (staging): 203.0.113.0/28

Question on service accounts: we typically namespace as svc-redwood-<env>-<purpose> (e.g., svc-redwood-staging-provision). Is that compatible? Also want to confirm whether Redwood issues long-lived API keys or recommends short-lived tokens with rotation via our KMS.

I'll loop in Raj (our infra lead) for the prod IP list and to coordinate any firewall changes. Meeting on Tue works for us; send a couple of times and we will confirm.

Thanks,

Elena Garcia
Director, IT Security
AcmeCorp
[Attachment: acme-saml-metadata.xml]
[Attachment: partial-ip-allowlist.csv]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T13:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation orchestration: enterprise access checklist & staging plan

Mateo/Monica — quick internal note.

We should sequence this so SCIM provisioning and SAML attribute mapping are validated in parallel but gated by the IP allowlist confirmation. Engineering will want a short lived token approach (recommended) — we can provide a small sidecar that exchanges a long-lived client credential for a short-lived token if they require KMS-backed rotation. That keeps us compliant and reduces support churn.

I'll draft the minimal scope for the SCIM admin (users:read, users:write, groups:read) and send to Mateo for approval before we share with Acme.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation orchestration: enterprise access checklist & staging plan

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping Raj.

I put together a short mutual action plan below (high level):
- 9/14–9/16: Customer provides SAML metadata + SCIM admin + staging IPs (DONE: partial)
- 9/17: Redwood validates SAML metadata in staging and returns attribute map
- 9/20: Dry-run SCIM provisioning and SAML login test in staging (2-hour window)
- 9/27: Production cutover window (requires prod IPs + change window approval from Acme networking)

Open items for Acme:
- Prod IP ranges (Raj please confirm)
- Confirmation on service account naming convention (svc-redwood-<env>-<purpose> is fine for us)
- Which attributes do you expect mapped to your HR system? (sAMAccountName, mail, employeeId)

I've attached the Doc with proposed attribute mappings and a calendar poll link — please pick two preferred slots for the dry-run:
https://drive.google.com/example-implementation-plan

If prod firewall changes take longer, we can do a gradual fallback: keep staging SSO available and use token-based authentication for a short period.

Thanks — I'll send the calendar invite once a slot is selected.

Cheers,

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
[Related: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/9817]

From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@acmecorp.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-09-16T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation orchestration: enterprise access checklist & staging plan

Monica — thanks, that plan looks good. Raj confirmed prod IP ranges (will forward the finalized list by EOD tomorrow) and we've created the SCIM service principal (scim-admin@acmecorp.com). We are aligned on the service account naming convention.

We picked the 9/20 10:00–12:00 slot for the dry-run. Raj and I will join; Ben, can you include your eng contact for the sidecar token exchange discussion? Also we are tracking approvals — procurement flagged one compliance form but it shouldn't block the staging run.

See you on 9/20.

Elena

Elena Garcia
Director, IT Security
AcmeCorp
